title: categories.children
description: One rung of the category cascade: the ACTIVE children of a node, in storefront order. This object validates the request payload; the response is {"parent_id": <int|null>, "children": [Child]} — see $defs.Child. parent_id null (or absent) asks for the active roots. Rows are active, non-deleted categories only, ordered exactly as the public tree HTTP views order the cascade (tn_priority descending, then id), so an agent walking the tree sees the same rungs in the same order a person sees in the storefront. Each Child carries children_count — its own number of ACTIVE children, 0 meaning leaf — so the walker knows it hit bottom without a second call. A parent_id that names no walkable node (unknown, inactive or deleted) raises LookupError, the categories.features convention: "no such rung" is an error, a leaf is an empty list. Names are display names (the configured DISPLAY_TRANSLATOR applied), not raw translation keys.

parent_id.description: ID of the node whose children to list; null (or absent) means the active roots — the cascade's first rung.

Child.description: One rung in the response 'children' array.

id.description: Category id — feed it back as the next parent_id to descend.

slug.description: The storefront's URL vocabulary for this node.

children_count.description: How many ACTIVE, non-deleted children this child has. 0 means leaf — descending further raises nothing, there is simply no rung to ask for.
